# aeneid-089 — new house renderings proposed

| line | Latin | `l` | `i` |
|---|---|---|---|
| XI.831 (= XII.952) | *vitaque cum gemitu fugit indignata sub umbras* | "and life with a groan takes flight, chafing, down under the shades." | "and life, bitter at its going, took flight with a groan down among the shades." |

Built from the Latin. `indignata` means resenting, deeming its end unworthy (L&S *indignor*). `fugit` is the present, as the metre shows (short *u*: vī-tă-quĕ | cūm gĕ-mĭ | tū fŭ-gĭt), so `l` has "takes flight". `i` is in the past because the surrounding narrative in `i` is. *sub umbras* is an accusative of motion. It is "down under the shades" in `l`, after the house IV.660 `l` "to go under the shades", and "down among the shades" in `i`, after the house IV.660 `i` "to go down among the shades". So the two lines where Virgil uses *sub umbras* of a death read alike.

Checked against memory of the best-known modern versions for distinctive echoes. The rendering avoids "fled", "resentful(ly)", "indignant", "outrage(d)", "indignity", "disdainful", "moan", "protesting" and the collocations "fled … down to the shades", "shades below" and "dark below". "With a groan" is kept because *cum gemitu* allows nothing else.

**Reviewer's change from the drafter's proposal.** The drafter's `i` was "and life, crying out against its lot, passed with a groan into the world of shades." It was replaced for two reasons:
- "crying out" repeats *cum gemitu* and misreads *indignata*, which is resentment, not a cry;
- "passed" loses the flight of *fugit*.

In `l`, "beneath" became "down under", to match IV.660 and show the motion.

The `i` is gender-neutral ("life", "its going"), so it serves unchanged for Turnus at XII.952. Only the tense of the surrounding sentence may need to match there.

No other new house renderings: no other line in XI.725–835 is a listed set piece.
